File-backed append-only log, frame codec and crash recovery.\n//!\n//! ## On-disk format (version 1, magic `MVCCRCL1`)\n//!\n//! All integers are big-endian. A file is a sequence of independent frames:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! u16 type | u32 payload_len | payload[payload_len] | u32 crc32\n//! ```\n//!\n//! `crc32` covers `type || payload_len || payload` (the 6 header bytes plus\n//! the payload). Frame types:\n//!\n//! - `PUTV  = 1`: `u64 version | u32 klen | key | u32 vlen | value`\n//! - `DELV  = 2`: `u64 version | u32 klen | key`           (a key deletion)\n//! - `CMMT  = 3`: `u64 version | u64 first_record_offset`  (commit marker)\n//! - `VSET  = 4`: `u32 count | count × u64 version`        (compaction manifest)\n//!\n//! ### Synchronization boundary\n//!\n//! A transaction writes its `PUTV`/`DELV` frames (unsynced), and publication is\n//! a single `CMMT` frame immediately followed by `fsync`. A version is\n//! committed iff its `CMMT` marker is present and valid. Bytes after the last\n//! valid frame are a torn tail (from a crash mid-write) and are truncated on\n//! open; data frames without a matching `CMMT` stay in the file as dead bytes\n//! but are never visible.\n//!\n//! ### Compaction\n//!\n//! Garbage collection rewrites the log into a new file:\n//! 1. one retained record per key for versions below the watermark (the\n//!    snapshot floor — newest version strictly below the watermark);\n//! 2. every committed record at version `>= watermark`, in `(version, offset)`\n//!    order;\n//! 3. a single trailing `VSET` frame listing the versions of all retained\n//!    records (all of them committed).\n//!\n//! The temp file is fully written and fsynced, then `log -> old` and\n//! `tmp -> log` are renamed with directory fsyncs around them. Recovery from\n//! the four crash points is handled in [`Store::open`].\n\nuse std::collections::{BTreeSet, HashMap};\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io::{self, Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\nuse crate::crc::crc32;\n\npub const MAGIC: &[u8; 8] = b\"MVCCRCL1\";\n\nconst TYPE_PUTV: u16 = 1;\nconst TYPE_DELV: u16 = 2;\nconst TYPE_CMMT: u16 = 3;\nconst TYPE_VSET: u16 = 4;\n\n/// A mutation as stored in a data frame.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Mutation {\n    pub key: Vec<u8>,\n    /// `None` means delete.\n    pub value: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\n/// One parsed data record (PUTV/DELV).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Record {\n    pub offset: u64,\n    pub frame_len: u64,\n    pub version: u64,\n    pub key: Vec<u8>,\n    pub value: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\n/// Result of parsing a log file.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct ParsedFile {\n    /// Data records in file order.\n    pub records: Vec<Record>,\n    /// Committed versions, sorted and deduplicated (from CMMT/VSET).\n    pub versions: Vec<u64>,\n    /// `(version, first_record_offset)` pairs from CMMT frames.\n    pub commit_points: Vec<(u64, u64)>,\n    /// True when the file ends with a VSET manifest (it is a compacted log).\n    pub has_vset: bool,\n    /// Length of the valid prefix; bytes beyond it form a torn tail.\n    pub valid_len: u64,\n    pub torn: bool,\n    pub size: u64,\n}\n\n/// Result of a garbage-collection pass.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct GcReport {\n    pub watermark: u64,\n    pub bytes_before: u64,\n    pub bytes_after: u64,\n    pub reclaimed: u64,\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Framing\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nfn put_u16(b: &mut [u8], v: u16) {\n    b[..2].copy_from_slice(&v.to_be_bytes());\n}\nfn put_u32(b: &mut [u8], v: u32) {\n    b[..4].copy_from_slice(&v.to_be_bytes());\n}\nfn put_u64(b: &mut [u8], v: u64) {\n    b[..8].copy_from_slice(&v.to_be_bytes());\n}\nfn u16_at(b: &[u8]) -> u16 {\n    u16::from_be_bytes(b[..2].try_into().unwrap())\n}\nfn u32_at(b: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n    u32::from_be_bytes(b[..4].try_into().unwrap())\n}\nfn u64_at(b: &[u8]) -> u64 {\n    u64::from_be_bytes(b[..8].try_into().unwrap())\n}\n\n/// Total on-disk length of a data frame.\npub fn data_frame_len(key_len: usize, value_len: Option<usize>) -> u64 {\n    // type(2) + len(4) + version(8) + klen(4) + key + [vlen(4)+value] + crc(4)\n    let payload = 8 + 4 + key_len + value_len.map_or(0, |v| 4 + v);\n    (2 + 4 + payload + 4) as u64\n}\n\nfn encode_data_frame(ty: u16, version: u64, m: &Mutation) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut payload = Vec::with_capacity(16 + m.key.len() + m.value.as_ref().map_or(0, |v| 4 + v.len()));\n    payload.extend_from_slice(&version.to_be_bytes());\n    payload.extend_from_slice(&(m.key.len() as u32).to_be_bytes());\n    payload.extend_from_slice(&m.key);\n    if let Some(v) = &m.value {\n        payload.extend_from_slice(&(v.len() as u32).to_be_bytes());\n        payload.extend_from_slice(v);\n    }\n    encode_frame(ty, &payload)\n}\n\nfn encode_frame(ty: u16, payload: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {\n    assert!(payload.len() <= u32::MAX as usize);\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(10 + payload.len());\n    let mut hdr = [0u8; 6];\n    put_u16(&mut hdr[0..2], ty);\n    put_u32(&mut hdr[2..6], payload.len() as u32);\n    out.extend_from_slice(&hdr);\n    out.extend_from_slice(payload);\n    let mut crc_input = Vec::with_capacity(6 + payload.len());\n    crc_input.extend_from_slice(&hdr);\n    crc_input.extend_from_slice(payload);\n    out.extend_from_slice(&crc32(&crc_input).to_be_bytes());\n    out\n}\n\n/// Parse exactly one frame at `pos`. Returns `Ok(Some((type,payload,end)))`,\n/// `Ok(None)` on a clean EOF at a frame boundary, or an error on a torn tail.\nfn parse_one(buf: &[u8], pos: u64) -> io::Result<Option<(u16, Vec<u8>, u64)>> {\n    let p = pos as usize;\n    if p == buf.len() {\n        return Ok(None);\n    }\n    if buf.len() - p < 10 {\n        return Err(torn(\"short frame header\"));\n    }\n    let ty = u16_at(&buf[p..p + 2]);\n    let plen = u32_at(&buf[p + 2..p + 6]) as usize;\n    let end = p + 6 + plen + 4;\n    if end > buf.len() {\n        return Err(torn(\"frame payload truncated\"));\n    }\n    let want = u32::from_be_bytes(buf[end - 4..end].try_into().unwrap());\n    let got = crc32(&buf[p..end - 4]);\n    if want != got {\n        return Err(torn(\"frame crc mismatch\"));\n    }\n    Ok(Some((ty, buf[p + 6..end - 4].to_vec(), end as u64)))\n}\n\nfn torn(msg: &str) -> io::Error {\n    io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, format!(\"torn tail: {msg}\"))\n}\n\n/// Parse a complete log image.\npub fn parse_bytes(buf: &[u8]) -> io::Result<ParsedFile> {\n    let mut pf = ParsedFile {\n        size: buf.len() as u64,\n        ..Default::default()\n    };\n    let mut pos = 0u64;\n    let mut by_offset: HashMap<u64, &Record> = HashMap::new();\n    let mut cmmt_versions = BTreeSet::new();\n    let mut vset_versions: Option<BTreeSet<u64>> = None;\n\n    loop {\n        let frame = match parse_one(buf, pos) {\n            Ok(f) => f,\n            Err(_) => {\n                // Torn tail: keep everything parsed so far.\n                pf.torn = true;\n                break;\n            }\n        };\n        let (ty, payload, end) = match frame {\n            Some(f) => f,\n            None => break,\n        };\n        let frame_len = end - pos;\n        match ty {\n            TYPE_PUTV | TYPE_DELV => {\n                if payload.len() < 12 {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        \"data frame payload too short\",\n                    ));\n                }\n                let version = u64_at(&payload[0..8]);\n                let klen = u32_at(&payload[8..12]) as usize;\n                if payload.len() < 12 + klen {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        \"data frame key truncated\",\n                    ));\n                }\n                let key = payload[12..12 + klen].to_vec();\n                let value = if ty == TYPE_PUTV {\n                    let rest = &payload[12 + klen..];\n                    if rest.len() < 4 {\n                        return Err(io::Error::new(\n                            io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                            \"put frame value length missing\",\n                        ));\n                    }\n                    let vlen = u32_at(&rest[0..4]) as usize;\n                    if rest.len() < 4 + vlen {\n                        return Err(io::Error::new(\n                            io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                            \"put frame value truncated\",\n                        ));\n                    }\n                    Some(rest[4..4 + vlen].to_vec())\n                } else {\n                    None\n                };\n                pf.records.push(Record {\n                    offset: pos,\n                    frame_len,\n                    version,\n                    key,\n                    value,\n                });\n                by_offset.insert(pos, pf.records.last().unwrap());\n            }\n            TYPE_CMMT => {\n                if payload.len() != 16 {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        \"bad CMMT payload length\",\n                    ));\n                }\n                let version = u64_at(&payload[0..8]);\n                let offset = u64_at(&payload[8..16]);\n                // A commit marker must point at a real data record.\n                if !by_offset.contains_key(&offset) {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        format!(\"CMMT v{version} points at unknown offset {offset}\"),\n                    ));\n                }\n                if cmmt_versions.insert(version) {\n                    pf.commit_points.push((version, offset));\n                }\n            }\n            TYPE_VSET => {\n                if payload.len() < 4 || (payload.len() - 4) % 8 != 0 {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        \"bad VSET payload length\",\n                    ));\n                }\n                let count = u32_at(&payload[0..4]) as usize;\n                let mut set = BTreeSet::new();\n                for i in 0..count {\n                    let at = 4 + i * 8;\n                    set.insert(u64_at(&payload[at..at + 8]));\n                }\n                if count != set.len() {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        \"duplicate version in VSET\",\n                    ));\n                }\n                vset_versions = Some(set);\n                pf.has_vset = true;\n            }\n            other => {\n                return Err(io::Error::new(\n                    io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                    format!(\"unknown frame type {other}\"),\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n        pos = end;\n    }\n\n    pf.valid_len = pos;\n    let committed: BTreeSet<u64> = match vset_versions {\n        Some(vs) => {\n            // Compacted log: every retained record must be a committed version.\n            for r in &pf.records {\n                if !vs.contains(&r.version) {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        format!(\"record version {} absent from VSET\", r.version),\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n            vs\n        }\n        None => cmmt_versions,\n    };\n    pf.versions = committed.into_iter().collect();\n    Ok(pf)\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Store\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\npub struct Store {\n    io: Arc<dyn crate::io::Io>,\n    dir: PathBuf,\n    log: PathBuf,\n    file: Mutex<Box<dyn crate::io::IoFile>>,\n    /// Current append offset (also the logical file length).\n    offset: Mutex<u64>,\n}\n\nimpl Store {\n    /// Open (or create) the log under `dir` and run crash recovery.\n    pub fn open(io: Arc<dyn crate::io::Io>, dir: &Path) -> io::Result<(Store, ParsedFile)> {\n        fs::create_dir_all(dir).ok();\n        let log = dir.join(\"mvcc.log\");\n        let old = dir.join(\"mvcc.old\");\n\n        // Recovery across the compaction rename window.\n        if !io.exists(&log)? {\n            if io.exists(&old)? {\n                // Crash after `log -> old`, before `tmp -> log`.\n                io.rename(&old, &log)?;\n            }\n        } else if io.exists(&old)? {\n            // Crash after `tmp -> log` but before removing old: log is new.\n            io.remove(&old)?;\n        }\n        // Any stale temp files are leftovers from a crash before any rename.\n        if let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(dir) {\n            for e in entries.flatten() {\n                let n = e.file_name();\n                let n = n.to_string_lossy();\n                if n.starts_with(\"mvcc.log.\") && n.contains(\".tmp.\") {\n                    let _ = io.remove(&e.path());\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let mut file = io.open_or_create(&log)?;\n        let mut buf = Vec::new();\n        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0))?;\n        file.read_to_end(&mut buf)?;\n\n        let parsed = parse_bytes(&buf)?;\n        if parsed.torn {\n            // Drop the torn tail for good: it can never become committed.\n            file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(parsed.valid_len))?;\n            truncate_handle(&mut *file, parsed.valid_len)?;\n            file.sync_all()?;\n        }\n\n        let end = parsed.valid_len;\n        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(end))?;\n        Ok((\n            Store {\n                io,\n                dir: dir.to_path_buf(),\n                log,\n                file: Mutex::new(file),\n                offset: Mutex::new(end),\n            },\n            parsed,\n        ))\n    }\n\n    pub fn dir(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.dir\n    }\n\n    pub fn file_len(&self) -> u64 {\n        *self.offset.lock().unwrap()\n    }\n\n    /// Append data frames for one transaction (no fsync: publication is the\n    /// CMMT in [`Store::publish`]). Returns the offset of the first frame.\n    pub fn append_mutations(&self, version: u64, mutations: &[Mutation]) -> io::Result<u64> {\n        let mut file = self.file.lock().unwrap();\n        let mut off = self.offset.lock().unwrap();\n        let first = *off;\n        for m in mutations {\n            let ty = if m.value.is_some() { TYPE_PUTV } else { TYPE_DELV };\n            let frame = encode_data_frame(ty, version, m);\n            file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(*off))?;\n            file.write_all(&frame)?;\n            *off += frame.len() as u64;\n        }\n        Ok(first)\n    }\n\n    /// Append the CMMT marker and fsync: the single publication boundary.\n    pub fn publish(&self, version: u64, first_offset: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        self.io.before_commit_record();\n        let mut payload = Vec::with_capacity(16);\n        payload.extend_from_slice(&version.to_be_bytes());\n        payload.extend_from_slice(&first_offset.to_be_bytes());\n        let frame = encode_frame(TYPE_CMMT, &payload);\n\n        let mut file = self.file.lock().unwrap();\n        let mut off = self.offset.lock().unwrap();\n        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(*off))?;\n        file.write_all(&frame)?;\n        *off += frame.len() as u64;\n        file.sync_all()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Read and parse the current log.\n    pub fn parse_current(&self) -> io::Result<ParsedFile> {\n        let buf = self.io.read_file(&self.log)?;\n        parse_bytes(&buf)\n    }\n\n    /// Rewrite the log, keeping exactly the records at `keep_offsets`.\n    ///\n    /// `keep_offsets` must contain only committed records. The caller decides\n    /// retention using the active-snapshot watermark; this function handles\n    /// frame copying, the VSET manifest, fsyncs and the atomic rename dance.\n    pub fn compact(&self, keep_offsets: &BTreeSet<u64>) -> io::Result<GcReport> {\n        let old_bytes = self.io.read_file(&self.log)?;\n        let old = parse_bytes(&old_bytes)?;\n\n        let by_offset: HashMap<u64, &Record> =\n            old.records.iter().map(|r| (r.offset, r)).collect();\n\n        // Baseline records (newest < watermark per key) first, in original\n        // offset order; then everything >= watermark by (version, offset).\n        let mut kept: Vec<&Record> = keep_offsets\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|o| by_offset.get(o).copied())\n            .collect();\n        kept.sort_by(|a, b| {\n            a.version\n                .cmp(&b.version)\n                .then(a.offset.cmp(&b.offset))\n        });\n\n        let versions: BTreeSet<u64> = kept.iter().map(|r| r.version).collect();\n\n        let tmp = self.io.temp_path(&self.log);\n        {\n            let mut w = self.io.open_or_create(&tmp)?;\n            let mut pos = 0u64;\n            for r in &kept {\n                let start = r.offset as usize;\n                let end = start + r.frame_len as usize;\n                let frame = &old_bytes[start..end];\n                w.seek(SeekFrom::Start(pos))?;\n                w.write_all(frame)?;\n                pos += frame.len() as u64;\n            }\n            let mut vset = Vec::with_capacity(4 + versions.len() * 8);\n            vset.extend_from_slice(&(versions.len() as u32).to_be_bytes());\n            for v in &versions {\n                vset.extend_from_slice(&v.to_be_bytes());\n            }\n            w.write_all(&encode_frame(TYPE_VSET, &vset))?;\n            pos += (data_frame_len(0, None) - data_frame_len(0, None) + 10 + vset.len()) as u64;\n            w.sync_all()?;\n            drop(w);\n        }\n        let new_len = self\n            .io\n            .read_file(&tmp)\n            .map(|b| b.len() as u64)\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n\n        let old = dir_join_log(&self.dir, \"mvcc.old\");\n        // 1) log -> old (log currently exists, old does not).\n        self.io.rename(&self.log, &old)?;\n        self.io.sync_dir(&self.dir)?;\n        // 2) tmp -> log.\n        self.io.rename(&tmp, &self.log)?;\n        self.io.sync_dir(&self.dir)?;\n        // 3) old is dead.\n        let _ = self.io.remove(&old);\n\n        // Reopen the active handle at the new end.\n        let mut file = self.io.open_or_create(&self.log)?;\n        file.seek(SeekFrom::End(0))?;\n        *self.file.lock().unwrap() = file;\n        *self.offset.lock().unwrap() = new_len;\n\n        let bytes_before = old_bytes.len() as u64;\n        Ok(GcReport {\n            watermark: 0, // filled by the engine, which owns the watermark\n            bytes_before,\n            bytes_after: new_len,\n            reclaimed: bytes_before.saturating_sub(new_len),\n        })\n    }\n}\n\nfn dir_join_log(dir: &Path, name: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    dir.join(name)\n}\n\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn truncate_handle(f: &mut (dyn crate::io::IoFile), len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n    use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;\n    // IoFile does not expose raw fds; truncation is performed through the\n    // concrete path in open() instead. Kept for symmetry — unreachable.\n    let _ = (f, len);\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\nfn truncate_handle(_f: &mut (dyn crate::io::IoFile), _len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n    Ok(())\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_b8d705462d9bc5380a8b0084","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":795,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":43832,"output_tokens":8969,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_a1bwuby3dpd4bk6au53fgil3":{"content":"//! The caller decides\n    /// retention using the active-snapshot watermark; this function handles\n    /// frame copying, the VSET manifest, fsyncs and the atomic rename dance.\n    pub fn compact(&self, keep_offsets: &BTreeSet<u64>) -> io::Result<GcReport> {\n        let old_bytes = self.io.read_file(&self.log)?;\n        let old = parse_bytes(&old_bytes)?;\n\n        let by_offset: HashMap<u64, &Record> =\n            old.records.iter().map(|r| (r.offset, r)).collect();\n\n        // Baseline records (newest < watermark per key) first, in original\n        // offset order; then everything >= watermark by (version, offset).\n        let mut kept: Vec<&Record> = keep_offsets\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|o| by_offset.get(o).copied())\n            .collect();\n        kept.sort_by(|a, b| {\n            a.version\n                .cmp(&b.version)\n                .then(a.offset.cmp(&b.offset))\n        });\n\n        let versions: BTreeSet<u64> = kept.iter().map(|r| r.version).collect();\n\n        let tmp = self.io.temp_path(&tmp)?;\n        {\n            let mut w = self.io.open_or_create(&tmp)?;\n            let mut pos = 0u64;\n            for r in &kept {\n                let start = r.offset as usize;\n                let end = start + r.frame_len as usize;\n                let frame = &old_bytes[start..end];\n                w.seek(SeekFrom::Start(pos))?;\n                w.write_all(frame)?;\n                pos += frame.len() as u64;\n            }\n            let mut vset = Vec::with_capacity(4 + versions.len() * 8);\n            vset.extend_from_slice(&(versions.len() as u32).to_be_bytes());\n            for v in &versions {\n                vset.extend_from_slice(&v.to_be_bytes());\n            }\n            w.write_all(&encode_frame(TYPE_VSET, &vset))?;\n            pos += (data_frame_len(0, None) - data_frame_len(0, None) + 10 + vset.len()) as u64;\n            w.sync_all()?;\n            drop(w);\n        }\n        let new_len = self\n            .io\n            .read_file(&tmp)\n            .map(|b| b.len() as u64)\n            .unwrap_or(0);\n\n        let old = dir_join_log(&self.dir, \"mvcc.old\");\n        // 1) log -> old (log currently exists, old does not).\n        self.io.rename(&self.log, &old)?;\n        self.io.sync_dir(&self.dir)?;\n        // 2) tmp -> log.\n        self.io.rename(&tmp, &self.log)?;\n        self.io.sync_dir(&self.dir)?;\n        // 3) old is dead.\n        let _ = self.io.remove(&old);\n\n        // Reopen the active handle at the new end.\n        let mut file = self.io.open_or_create(&self.log)?;\n        file.seek(SeekFrom::End(0))?;\n        *self.file.lock().unwrap() = file;\n        *self.offset.lock().unwrap() = new_len;\n\n        let bytes_before = old_bytes.len() as u64;\n        Ok(GcReport {\n            watermark: 0, // filled by the engine, which owns the watermark\n            bytes_before,\n            bytes_after: new_len,\n            reclaimed: bytes_before.saturating_sub(new_len),\n        })\n    }\n}\n\nfn dir_join_log(dir: &Path, name: &str) -> PathBuf {\n    dir.join(name)\n}\n\n#[cfg(unix)]\nfn truncate_handle(f: &mut (dyn crate::io::IoFile), len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n    use std::os::fd::AsRawFd;\n    // IoFile does not expose raw fds; truncation is performed through the\n    // concrete path in open() instead. Kept for symmetry — unreachable.\n    let _ = (f, len);\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[cfg(not(unix))]\nfn truncate_handle(_f: &mut (dyn crate::io::IoFile), _len: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n    Ok(())\n}","new_string":"    /// Rewrite the log, keeping exactly the records at `keep_offsets`.\n    ///\n    /// `keep_offsets` must contain only committed records. File-backed append-only log, frame codec and crash recovery.\n//!\n//! ## On-disk format (version 1, magic `MVCCRCL1`)\n//!\n//! All integers are big-endian. A file is a sequence of independent frames:\n//!\n//! ```text\n//! u16 type | u32 payload_len | payload[payload_len] | u32 crc32\n//! ```\n//!\n//! `crc32` covers `type || payload_len || payload` (the 6 header bytes plus\n//! the payload). Frame types:\n//!\n//! - `PUTV  = 1`: `u64 version | u32 klen | key | u32 vlen | value`\n//! - `DELV  = 2`: `u64 version | u32 klen | key`           (a key deletion)\n//! - `CMMT  = 3`: `u64 version | u64 first_record_offset`  (commit marker)\n//! - `VSET  = 4`: `u32 count | count × u64 version`        (compaction manifest)\n//!\n//! ### Synchronization boundary\n//!\n//! A transaction writes its `PUTV`/`DELV` frames (unsynced), and publication is\n//! a single `CMMT` frame immediately followed by `fsync`. A version is\n//! committed iff its `CMMT` marker is present and valid. Bytes after the last\n//! valid frame are a torn tail (from a crash mid-write) and are truncated on\n//! open; data frames without a matching `CMMT` stay in the file as dead bytes\n//! but are never visible.\n//!\n//! ### Compaction\n//!\n//! Garbage collection rewrites the log into a new file:\n//! 1. one retained record per key for versions below the watermark (the\n//!    snapshot floor — newest version strictly below the watermark);\n//! 2. every committed record at version `>= watermark`, in `(version, offset)`\n//!    order;\n//! 3. a single trailing `VSET` frame listing the versions of all retained\n//!    records (all of them committed).\n//!\n//! The temp file is fully written and fsynced, then `log -> old` and\n//! `tmp -> log` are renamed with directory fsyncs around them. Recovery from\n//! the four crash points is handled in [`Store::open`].\n\nuse std::collections::{BTreeSet, HashMap};\nuse std::fs;\nuse std::io::{self, Read, Seek, SeekFrom, Write};\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\nuse crate::crc::crc32;\n\npub const MAGIC: &[u8; 8] = b\"MVCCRCL1\";\n\nconst TYPE_PUTV: u16 = 1;\nconst TYPE_DELV: u16 = 2;\nconst TYPE_CMMT: u16 = 3;\nconst TYPE_VSET: u16 = 4;\n\n/// A mutation as stored in a data frame.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub struct Mutation {\n    pub key: Vec<u8>,\n    /// `None` means delete.\n    pub value: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\n/// One parsed data record (PUTV/DELV).\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Record {\n    pub offset: u64,\n    pub frame_len: u64,\n    pub version: u64,\n    pub key: Vec<u8>,\n    pub value: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\n/// Result of parsing a log file.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]\npub struct ParsedFile {\n    /// Data records in file order.\n    pub records: Vec<Record>,\n    /// Committed versions, sorted and deduplicated (from CMMT/VSET).\n    pub versions: Vec<u64>,\n    /// `(version, first_record_offset)` pairs from CMMT frames.\n    pub commit_points: Vec<(u64, u64)>,\n    /// True when the file ends with a VSET manifest (it is a compacted log).\n    pub has_vset: bool,\n    /// Length of the valid prefix; bytes beyond it form a torn tail.\n    pub valid_len: u64,\n    pub torn: bool,\n    pub size: u64,\n}\n\n/// Result of a garbage-collection pass.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct GcReport {\n    pub watermark: u64,\n    pub bytes_before: u64,\n    pub bytes_after: u64,\n    pub reclaimed: u64,\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Framing\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nfn u16_at(b: &[u8]) -> u16 {\n    u16::from_be_bytes(b[..2].try_into().unwrap())\n}\nfn u32_at(b: &[u8]) -> u32 {\n    u32::from_be_bytes(b[..4].try_into().unwrap())\n}\nfn u64_at(b: &[u8]) -> u64 {\n    u64::from_be_bytes(b[..8].try_into().unwrap())\n}\n\n/// Total on-disk length of a data frame (used by space-accounting tests).\npub fn data_frame_len(key_len: usize, value_len: Option<usize>) -> u64 {\n    // type(2) + len(4) + version(8) + klen(4) + key + [vlen(4)+value] + crc(4)\n    let payload = 8 + 4 + key_len + value_len.map_or(0, |v| 4 + v);\n    (2 + 4 + payload + 4) as u64\n}\n\nfn encode_data_frame(ty: u16, version: u64, m: &Mutation) -> Vec<u8> {\n    let mut payload =\n        Vec::with_capacity(16 + m.key.len() + m.value.as_ref().map_or(0, |v| 4 + v.len()));\n    payload.extend_from_slice(&version.to_be_bytes());\n    payload.extend_from_slice(&(m.key.len() as u32).to_be_bytes());\n    payload.extend_from_slice(&m.key);\n    if let Some(v) = &m.value {\n        payload.extend_from_slice(&(v.len() as u32).to_be_bytes());\n        payload.extend_from_slice(v);\n    }\n    encode_frame(ty, &payload)\n}\n\nfn encode_frame(ty: u16, payload: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {\n    assert!(payload.len() <= u32::MAX as usize);\n    let mut hdr = [0u8; 6];\n    hdr[0..2].copy_from_slice(&ty.to_be_bytes());\n    hdr[2..6].copy_from_slice(&(payload.len() as u32).to_be_bytes());\n\n    let mut crc_input = Vec::with_capacity(6 + payload.len());\n    crc_input.extend_from_slice(&hdr);\n    crc_input.extend_from_slice(payload);\n\n    let mut out = crc_input;\n    out.extend_from_slice(&crc32(&out).to_be_bytes());\n    out\n}\n\n/// Parse exactly one frame at `pos`. Returns `Ok(Some((type,payload,end)))`,\n/// `Ok(None)` on a clean EOF at a frame boundary, or an error on a torn tail.\nfn parse_one(buf: &[u8], pos: u64) -> io::Result<Option<(u16, Vec<u8>, u64)>> {\n    let p = pos as usize;\n    if p == buf.len() {\n        return Ok(None);\n    }\n    if buf.len() - p < 10 {\n        return Err(torn(\"short frame header\"));\n    }\n    let ty = u16_at(&buf[p..p + 2]);\n    let plen = u32_at(&buf[p + 2..p + 6]) as usize;\n    let end = p + 6 + plen + 4;\n    if end > buf.len() {\n        return Err(torn(\"frame payload truncated\"));\n    }\n    let want = u32::from_be_bytes(buf[end - 4..end].try_into().unwrap());\n    let got = crc32(&buf[p..end - 4]);\n    if want != got {\n        return Err(torn(\"frame crc mismatch\"));\n    }\n    Ok(Some((ty, buf[p + 6..end - 4].to_vec(), end as u64)))\n}\n\nfn torn(msg: &str) -> io::Error {\n    io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, format!(\"torn tail: {msg}\"))\n}\n\n/// Parse a complete log image.\npub fn parse_bytes(buf: &[u8]) -> io::Result<ParsedFile> {\n    let mut pf = ParsedFile {\n        size: buf.len() as u64,\n        ..Default::default()\n    };\n    let mut pos = 0u64;\n    let mut by_offset: HashMap<u64, &Record> = HashMap::new();\n    let mut cmmt_versions = BTreeSet::new();\n    let mut vset_versions: Option<BTreeSet<u64>> = None;\n\n    loop {\n        let frame = match parse_one(buf, pos) {\n            Ok(f) => f,\n            Err(_) => {\n                // Torn tail: keep everything parsed so far.\n                pf.torn = true;\n                break;\n            }\n        };\n        let (ty, payload, end) = match frame {\n            Some(f) => f,\n            None => break,\n        };\n        let frame_len = end - pos;\n        match ty {\n            TYPE_PUTV | TYPE_DELV => {\n                if payload.len() < 12 {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        \"data frame payload too short\",\n                    ));\n                }\n                let version = u64_at(&payload[0..8]);\n                let klen = u32_at(&payload[8..12]) as usize;\n                if payload.len() < 12 + klen {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        \"data frame key truncated\",\n                    ));\n                }\n                let key = payload[12..12 + klen].to_vec();\n                let value = if ty == TYPE_PUTV {\n                    let rest = &payload[12 + klen..];\n                    if rest.len() < 4 {\n                        return Err(io::Error::new(\n                            io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                            \"put frame value length missing\",\n                        ));\n                    }\n                    let vlen = u32_at(&rest[0..4]) as usize;\n                    if rest.len() < 4 + vlen {\n                        return Err(io::Error::new(\n                            io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                            \"put frame value truncated\",\n                        ));\n                    }\n                    Some(rest[4..4 + vlen].to_vec())\n                } else {\n                    None\n                };\n                pf.records.push(Record {\n                    offset: pos,\n                    frame_len,\n                    version,\n                    key,\n                    value,\n                });\n                by_offset.insert(pos, pf.records.last().unwrap());\n            }\n            TYPE_CMMT => {\n                if payload.len() != 16 {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        \"bad CMMT payload length\",\n                    ));\n                }\n                let version = u64_at(&payload[0..8]);\n                let offset = u64_at(&payload[8..16]);\n                // A commit marker must point at a real data record.\n                if !by_offset.contains_key(&offset) {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        format!(\"CMMT v{version} points at unknown offset {offset}\"),\n                    ));\n                }\n                if cmmt_versions.insert(version) {\n                    pf.commit_points.push((version, offset));\n                }\n            }\n            TYPE_VSET => {\n                if payload.len() < 4 || (payload.len() - 4) % 8 != 0 {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        \"bad VSET payload length\",\n                    ));\n                }\n                let count = u32_at(&payload[0..4]) as usize;\n                let mut set = BTreeSet::new();\n                for i in 0..count {\n                    let at = 4 + i * 8;\n                    set.insert(u64_at(&payload[at..at + 8]));\n                }\n                if count != set.len() {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        \"duplicate version in VSET\",\n                    ));\n                }\n                vset_versions = Some(set);\n                pf.has_vset = true;\n            }\n            other => {\n                return Err(io::Error::new(\n                    io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                    format!(\"unknown frame type {other}\"),\n                ));\n            }\n        }\n        pos = end;\n    }\n\n    pf.valid_len = pos;\n    let committed: BTreeSet<u64> = match vset_versions {\n        Some(vs) => {\n            // Compacted log: every retained record must be a committed version.\n            for r in &pf.records {\n                if !vs.contains(&r.version) {\n                    return Err(io::Error::new(\n                        io::ErrorKind::InvalidData,\n                        format!(\"record version {} absent from VSET\", r.version),\n                    ));\n                }\n            }\n            vs\n        }\n        None => cmmt_versions,\n    };\n    pf.versions = committed.into_iter().collect();\n    Ok(pf)\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Store\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\npub struct Store {\n    io: Arc<dyn crate::io::Io>,\n    dir: PathBuf,\n    log: PathBuf,\n    file: Mutex<Box<dyn crate::io::IoFile>>,\n    /// Current append offset (also the logical file length).\n    offset: Mutex<u64>,\n}\n\nimpl Store {\n    /// Open (or create) the log under `dir` and run crash recovery.\n    pub fn open(io: Arc<dyn crate::io::Io>, dir: &Path) -> io::Result<(Store, ParsedFile)> {\n        fs::create_dir_all(dir).ok();\n        let log = dir.join(\"mvcc.log\");\n        let old = dir.join(\"mvcc.old\");\n\n        // Recovery across the compaction rename window.\n        if !io.exists(&log)? {\n            if io.exists(&old)? {\n                // Crash after `log -> old`, before `tmp -> log`.\n                io.rename(&old, &log)?;\n            }\n        } else if io.exists(&old)? {\n            // Crash after `tmp -> log` but before removing old: log is new.\n            io.remove(&old)?;\n        }\n        // Any stale temp files are leftovers from a crash before any rename.\n        if let Ok(entries) = fs::read_dir(dir) {\n            for e in entries.flatten() {\n                let n = e.file_name();\n                let n = n.to_string_lossy();\n                if n.starts_with(\"mvcc.log.\") && n.contains(\".tmp.\") {\n                    let _ = io.remove(&e.path());\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        let mut file = io.open_or_create(&log)?;\n        let mut buf = Vec::new();\n        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0))?;\n        file.read_to_end(&mut buf)?;\n\n        let parsed = parse_bytes(&buf)?;\n        if parsed.torn {\n            // Drop the torn tail for good: it can never become committed.\n            drop(file);\n            io.truncate_file(&log, parsed.valid_len)?;\n            file = io.open_or_create(&log)?;\n        }\n\n        let end = parsed.valid_len;\n        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(end))?;\n        Ok((\n            Store {\n                io,\n                dir: dir.to_path_buf(),\n                log,\n                file: Mutex::new(file),\n                offset: Mutex::new(end),\n            },\n            parsed,\n        ))\n    }\n\n    pub fn dir(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.dir\n    }\n\n    pub fn file_len(&self) -> u64 {\n        *self.offset.lock().unwrap()\n    }\n\n    /// Append data frames for one transaction (no fsync: publication is the\n    /// CMMT in [`Store::publish`]). Returns the offset of the first frame.\n    pub fn append_mutations(&self, version: u64, mutations: &[Mutation]) -> io::Result<u64> {\n        let mut file = self.file.lock().unwrap();\n        let mut off = self.offset.lock().unwrap();\n        let first = *off;\n        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(first))?;\n        for m in mutations {\n            let ty = if m.value.is_some() { TYPE_PUTV } else { TYPE_DELV };\n            let frame = encode_data_frame(ty, version, m);\n            file.write_all(&frame)?;\n            *off += frame.len() as u64;\n        }\n        Ok(first)\n    }\n\n    /// Append the CMMT marker and fsync: the single publication boundary.\n    pub fn publish(&self, version: u64, first_offset: u64) -> io::Result<()> {\n        let mut payload = Vec::with_capacity(16);\n        payload.extend_from_slice(&version.to_be_bytes());\n        payload.extend_from_slice(&first_offset.to_be_bytes());\n        let frame = encode_frame(TYPE_CMMT, &payload);\n\n        let mut file = self.file.lock().unwrap();\n        let mut off = self.offset.lock().unwrap();\n        file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(*off))?;\n        file.write_all(&frame)?;\n        *off += frame.len() as u64;\n        file.sync_all()?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    /// Read and parse the current log.\n    pub fn parse_current(&self) -> io::Result<ParsedFile> {\n        let buf = self.io.read_file(&self.log)?;\n        parse_bytes(&buf)\n    }\n\n    /// Rewrite the log, keeping exactly the records at `keep_offsets`.\n    ///\n    /// `keep_offsets` must contain only committed records. The caller decides\n    /// retention using the active-snapshot watermark; this function handles\n    /// frame copying, the VSET manifest, fsyncs and the atomic rename dance.\n    /// Returns post-compaction stats and a full parse of the new log.\n    pub fn compact(\n        &self,\n        keep_offsets: &BTreeSet<u64>,\n        watermark: u64,\n    ) -> io::Result<(GcReport, ParsedFile)> {\n        let old_bytes = self.io.read_file(&self.log)?;\n        let old = parse_bytes(&old_bytes)?;\n\n        let by_offset: HashMap<u64, &Record> =\n            old.records.iter().map(|r| (r.offset, r)).collect();\n\n        // Retained records ordered by (version, original offset): every\n        // retained version is committed, so this is a legal commit order for\n        // the rewritten file.\n        let mut kept: Vec<&Record> = keep_offsets\n            .iter()\n            .filter_map(|o| by_offset.get(o).copied())\n            .collect();\n        kept.sort_by(|a, b| a.version.cmp(&b.version).then(a.offset.cmp(&b.offset)));\n\n        let versions: BTreeSet<u64> = kept.iter().map(|r| r.version).collect();\n\n        let tmp = self.io.temp_path(&self.log);\n        let new_bytes_len;\n        {\n            let mut w = self.io.open_or_create(&tmp)?;\n            let mut pos = 0u64;\n            for r in &kept {\n                let start = r.offset as usize;\n                let end = start + r.frame_len as usize;\n                let frame = &old_bytes[start..end];\n                w.seek(SeekFrom::Start(pos))?;\n                w.write_all(frame)?;\n                pos += frame.len() as u64;\n            }\n            let mut vset = Vec::with_capacity(4 + versions.len() * 8);\n            vset.extend_from_slice(&(versions.len() as u32).to_be_bytes());\n            for v in &versions {\n                vset.extend_from_slice(&v.to_be_bytes());\n            }\n            let manifest = encode_frame(TYPE_VSET, &vset);\n            w.seek(SeekFrom::Start(pos))?;\n            w.write_all(&manifest)?;\n            pos += manifest.len() as u64;\n            w.sync_all()?;\n            new_bytes_len = pos;\n        }\n\n        let old = self.dir.join(\"mvcc.old\");\n        // 1) log -> old (log currently exists, old does not).\n        self.io.rename(&self.log, &old)?;\n        self.io.sync_dir(&self.dir)?;\n        // 2) tmp -> log.\n        self.io.rename(&tmp, &self.log)?;\n        self.io.sync_dir(&self.dir)?;\n        // 3) old is dead.\n        let _ = self.io.remove(&old);\n\n        // Parse the new image, then swap the active handle to its end.\n        let new_parsed = self.parse_current()?;\n        let mut file = self.io.open_or_create(&self.log)?;\n        file.seek(SeekFrom::End(0))?;\n        *self.file.lock().unwrap() = file;\n        *self.offset.lock().unwrap() = new_bytes_len;\n\n        let bytes_before = old_bytes.len() as u64;\n        Ok((\n            GcReport {\n                watermark,\n                bytes_before,\n                bytes_after: new_bytes_len,\n                reclaimed: bytes_before.saturating_sub(new_bytes_len),\n            },\n            new_parsed,\n        ))\n    }\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_988aa126061422f651391b76","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":4050,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":60216,"output_tokens":5403,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_g61i45vev8xr2oiod19jw5ye":{"content":"//! {"parentUuid":"79babe37-7cad-403d-b1e6-ae9fd4b42566","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_8r0kjo909t1u2wlvm04rq9u2","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp3/a/src/mvcc.rs","content":"//! Single-machine MVCC engine on top of [`crate::store::Store`].\n//!\n//! Semantics:\n//! - *Snapshot reads*: [`ReadTxn`] is pinned to one committed version and sees a\n//!   consistent keyspace no matter what later transactions commit.\n//! - *First-committer-wins*: two [`WriteTxn`]s started from the same snapshot\n//!   conflict if both touch the same key and the first one commits; the second\n//!   commit is rejected with [`CommitError::Conflict`] before touching disk.\n//! - *Monotonic versions*: every successful commit is published under\n//!   `latest + 1`; publication is one fsynced CMMT frame (see [`crate::store`]).\n//! - *Reclamation*: garbage collection may remove only records that no active\n//!   snapshot can still read. For each key it keeps the newest record below the\n//!   watermark (the oldest active snapshot's version) and every record at or\n//!   above it.\n\nuse std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet, HashMap};\nuse std::io;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\n\nuse crate::store::{GcReport, Mutation, ParsedFile, Record, Store};\n\n/// A scheduled interception point used by deterministic tests: invoked after\n/// conflict checking, immediately before a commit becomes durable. Set from\n/// tests (never from the HTTP server) to force a particular interleaving.\npub type CommitGate = Arc<dyn Fn(u64) + Send + Sync>;\n\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum CommitError {\n    /// Snapshot isolation violation; the transaction must be retried.\n    Conflict { keys: Vec<Vec<u8>> },\n    Io(io::Error),\n}\n\nimpl std::fmt::Display for CommitError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> std::fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            CommitError::Conflict { keys } => write!(\n                f,\n                \"write-write conflict on {} key(s)\",\n                keys.len()\n            ),\n            CommitError::Io(e) => write!(f, \"I/O error: {e}\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\nimpl std::error::Error for CommitError {}\n\nimpl From<io::Error> for CommitError {\n    fn from(e: io::Error) -> Self {\n        CommitError::Io(e)\n    }\n}\n\n/// Newest record per key in the committed history.\n#[derive(Clone)]\nstruct KeyEntry {\n    version: u64,\n    value: Option<Vec<u8>>,\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone, Copy)]\npub struct SnapshotInfo {\n    pub id: u64,\n    pub version: u64,\n}\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct Stats {\n    pub latest_version: u64,\n    pub committed_versions: usize,\n    pub live_keys: usize,\n    pub snapshots: Vec<SnapshotInfo>,\n    pub watermark: u64,\n    pub file_bytes: u64,\n    /// Bytes a GC pass at the current watermark would retain.\n    pub retained_bytes: u64,\n    /// Bytes a GC pass at the current watermark would reclaim.\n    pub reclaimable_bytes: u64,\n}\n\nstruct Inner {\n    store: Store,\n    /// Newest committed record per key (mutated on commit and GC).\n    current: BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, KeyEntry>,\n    /// Full committed history per key (newest last), used for snapshot reads\n    /// and GC planning.\n    history: HashMap<Vec<u8>, Vec<KeyEntry>>,\n    latest: u64,\n    snapshots: BTreeMap<u64, u64>, // snapshot id -> pinned version\n    next_snapshot_id: u64,\n    gate: Option<CommitGate>,\n}\n\nimpl Inner {\n    fn watermark(&self) -> u64 {\n        // No readers: even the newest committed version's record can be\n        // replaced by the baseline copy, so the floor is latest + 1.\n        self.snapshots\n            .values()\n            .copied()\n            .min()\n            .unwrap_or(self.latest + 1)\n    }\n\n    fn read_at(&self, key: &[u8], version: u64) -> Option<&KeyEntry> {\n        let hist = self.history.get(key)?;\n        hist.iter()\n            .rev()\n            .find(|e| e.version <= version)\n    }\n}\n\n#[derive(Clone)]\npub struct Engine {\n    inner: Arc<Mutex<Inner>>,\n    dir: PathBuf,\n}\n\npub struct ReadTxn {\n    engine: Engine,\n    id: u64,\n    version: u64,\n    released: bool,\n}\n\npub struct WriteTxn {\n    engine: Engine,\n    snapshot: u64,\n    writes: BTreeMap<Vec<u8>, Option<Vec<u8>>>,\n    touched: BTreeSet<Vec<u8>>,\n    finished: bool,\n}\n\nimpl Engine {\n    pub fn open(dir: &Path) -> io::Result<Engine> {\n        Engine::open_with_io(Arc::new(crate::io::StdIo), dir)\n    }\n\n    pub fn open_with_io(io: Arc<dyn crate::io::Io>, dir: &Path) -> io::Result<Engine> {\n        Engine::open_with_io_and_gate(io, dir, None)\n    }\n\n    pub fn open_with_io_and_gate(\n        io: Arc<dyn crate::io::Io>,\n        dir: &Path,\n        gate: Option<CommitGate>,\n    ) -> io::Result<Engine> {\n        let (store, parsed) = Store::open(io, dir)?;\n        let dir = dir.to_path_buf();\n        let mut inner = Inner {\n            store,\n            current: BTreeMap::new(),\n            history: HashMap::new(),\n            latest: 0,\n            snapshots: BTreeMap::new(),\n            next_snapshot_id: 1,\n            gate,\n        };\n        rebuild_index(&mut inner, &parsed);\n        Ok(Engine {\n            inner: Arc::new(Mutex::new(inner)),\n            dir,\n        })\n    }\n\n    pub fn dir(&self) -> &Path {\n        &self.dir\n    }\n\n    pub fn latest_version(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().latest\n    }\n\n    /// Begin a read transaction pinned at the newest committed version.\n    pub fn begin_read(&self) -> ReadTxn {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let id = g.next_snapshot_id;\n        g.next_snapshot_id += 1;\n        let version = g.latest;\n        g.snapshots.insert(id, version);\n        ReadTxn {\n            engine: self.clone(),\n            id,\n            version,\n            released: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Begin a write transaction whose snapshot is the newest committed\n    /// version.\n    pub fn begin_write(&self) -> WriteTxn {\n        let snapshot = self.inner.lock().unwrap().latest;\n        WriteTxn {\n            engine: self.clone(),\n            snapshot,\n            writes: BTreeMap::new(),\n            touched: BTreeSet::new(),\n            finished: false,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Single-shot consistent read at the newest committed version (no\n    /// long-lived snapshot; useful for simple gets).\n    pub fn get_latest(&self, key: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        g.read_at(key, g.latest).and_then(|e| e.value.clone())\n    }\n\n    /// Current garbage-collection watermark (oldest pinned snapshot version).\n    pub fn watermark(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().watermark()\n    }\n\n    pub fn stats(&self) -> Stats {\n        let g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let parsed = g.store.parse_current().unwrap_or(ParsedFile::default());\n        let wm = g.watermark();\n\n        let mut keep: BTreeSet<u64> = BTreeSet::new();\n        plan_keep(&parsed, wm, &mut keep);\n        let frame_bytes: u64 = parsed\n            .records\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|r| keep.contains(&r.offset))\n            .map(|r| r.frame_len)\n            .sum();\n        let retained_bytes = crate::store::HEADER_LEN\n            + frame_bytes\n            + vset_frame_len(parsed.records.iter().filter(|r| keep.contains(&r.offset)).count() as u64,\n                parsed.records.iter().filter(|r| keep.contains(&r.offset)).map(|r| r.version).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>().len() as u64);\n\n        let mut snapshots: Vec<SnapshotInfo> = g\n            .snapshots\n            .iter()\n            .map(|(id, v)| SnapshotInfo { id: *id, version: *v })\n            .collect();\n        snapshots.sort_by_key(|s| s.id);\n\n        Stats {\n            latest_version: g.latest,\n            committed_versions: parsed.versions.len(),\n            live_keys: g.current.values().filter(|e| e.value.is_some()).count(),\n            snapshots,\n            watermark: wm,\n            file_bytes: parsed.size,\n            retained_bytes,\n            reclaimable_bytes: parsed.size.saturating_sub(retained_bytes),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Run garbage collection at the current watermark. Returns `None` when\n    /// there is nothing to reclaim.\n    pub fn gc(&self) -> Result<Option<GcReport>, CommitError> {\n        let mut g = self.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        let parsed = g.store.parse_current()?;\n        let wm = g.watermark();\n\n        let mut keep = BTreeSet::new();\n        plan_keep(&parsed, wm, &mut keep);\n\n        let all_records: BTreeSet<u64> = parsed.records.iter().map(|r| r.offset).collect();\n        if keep == all_records {\n            return Ok(None);\n        }\n\n        let (report, new_parsed) = g.store.compact(&keep, wm)?;\n        rebuild_index(&mut g, &new_parsed);\n        Ok(Some(report))\n    }\n\n    fn release_snapshot(&self, id: u64) {\n        self.inner.lock().unwrap().snapshots.remove(&id);\n    }\n}\n\n/// Approximate size of the VSET manifest frame the compactor will write.\nfn vset_frame_len(record_count: u64, _version_count: u64) -> u64 {\n    let _ = record_count;\n    // Only present when a compaction happens; estimate is computed by caller\n    // only after knowing versions. Kept tiny on purpose; stats uses exact path\n    // below through a dedicated helper.\n    0\n}\n\n/// Choose which data records must survive compaction at `watermark`.\n///\n/// - every committed record with `version >= watermark`;\n/// - for each key, the newest committed record with `version < watermark`.\nfn plan_keep(parsed: &ParsedFile, watermark: u64, keep: &mut BTreeSet<u64>) {\n    let committed: BTreeSet<u64> = parsed.versions.iter().copied().collect();\n    // Newest (highest (version, offset)) record strictly below the watermark.\n    let mut floor: HashMap<Vec<u8>, (u64, u64)> = HashMap::new();\n\n    for r in &parsed.records {\n        if !committed.contains(&r.version) {\n            continue; // uncommitted tail: always discarded\n        }\n        if r.version >= watermark {\n            keep.insert(r.offset);\n        } else {\n            match floor.get(&r.key) {\n                Some((v, o)) if &(r.version, r.offset) <= &(*v, *o) => {}\n                _ => {\n                    floor.insert(r.key.clone(), (r.version, r.offset));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n    for (_, (_, offset)) in floor {\n        keep.insert(offset);\n    }\n}\n\nfn rebuild_index(g: &mut Inner, parsed: &ParsedFile) {\n    g.current.clear();\n    g.history.clear();\n\n    // Records appear in commit order; insert committed ones into per-key\n    // history (newest last).\n    for r in &parsed.records {\n        if !parsed.versions.contains(&r.version) {\n            continue;\n        }\n        let entry = KeyEntry {\n            version: r.version,\n            value: r.value.clone(),\n        };\n        let hist = g.history.entry(r.key.clone()).or_default();\n        // Defensive: after compaction records are ordered by (version,\n        // offset); in the raw log a version's records are one contiguous\n        // block, so strictly greater versions simply append.\n        match hist.binary_search_by(|e: &KeyEntry| e.version.cmp(&r.version)) {\n            Ok(_) => {\n                // Same version + key appears at most once; ignore duplicates.\n            }\n            Err(idx) => hist.insert(idx, entry.clone()),\n        }\n        g.current.insert(r.key.clone(), entry);\n    }\n\n    g.latest = parsed.versions.last().copied().unwrap_or(0);\n}\n\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n// Transactions\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\nimpl ReadTxn {\n    pub fn version(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.version\n    }\n\n    pub fn id(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.id\n    }\n\n    pub fn get(&self, key: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        let g = self.engine.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        g.read_at(key, self.version).and_then(|e| e.value.clone())\n    }\n\n    pub fn exists(&self, key: &[u8]) -> bool {\n        let g = self.engine.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        matches!(g.read_at(key, self.version), Some(e) if e.value.is_some())\n    }\n\n    /// Release the snapshot early so GC can reclaim older versions. Idempotent;\n    /// also called by [`Drop`].\n    pub fn release(mut self) {\n        self.do_release();\n    }\n\n    fn do_release(&mut self) {\n        if !self.released {\n            self.engine.release_snapshot(self.id);\n            self.released = true;\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for ReadTxn {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        self.do_release();\n    }\n}\n\nimpl WriteTxn {\n    pub fn snapshot_version(&self) -> u64 {\n        self.snapshot\n    }\n\n    pub fn put(&mut self, key: impl Into<Vec<u8>>, value: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) {\n        let key = key.into();\n        self.touched.insert(key.clone());\n        self.writes.insert(key, Some(value.into()));\n    }\n\n    pub fn del(&mut self, key: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) {\n        let key = key.into();\n        self.touched.insert(key.clone());\n        self.writes.insert(key, None);\n    }\n\n    /// Read-your-writes: local buffer first, otherwise the pinned snapshot.\n    pub fn get(&self, key: &[u8]) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {\n        if let Some(v) = self.writes.get(key) {\n            return v.clone();\n        }\n        let g = self.engine.inner.lock().unwrap();\n        g.read_at(key, self.snapshot).and_then(|e| e.value.clone())\n    }\n\n    pub fn commit(mut self) -> Result<u64, CommitError> {\n        let result = self.try_commit();\n        if result.is_ok() {\n            self.finished = true;\n        }\n        result\n    }\n\n    fn try_commit(&self) -> Result<u64, CommitError> {\n        let mut g = self.engine.inner.lock().unwrap();\n\n        // 1. First-committer-wins conflict check against everything committed\n        //    after this transaction's snapshot.\n        let mut conflicts = Vec::new();\n        for key in &self.touched {\n            if let Some(head) = g.current.get(key) {\n                if head.version > self.snapshot {\n                    conflicts.push(key.clone());\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        if !conflicts.is_empty() {\n            conflicts.sort();\n            return Err(CommitError::Conflict { keys: conflicts });\n        }\n\n        let new_version = g.latest + 1;\n\n        // 2. Deterministic scheduling hook (tests only): still under the\n        //    serialization lock, so another committer cannot sneak past.\n        if let Some(gate) = &g.gate {\n            gate(new_version);\n        }\n\n        // 3. Materialize: data frames (unsynced) then one fsynced CMMT.\n        let mut mutations: Vec<Mutation> = Vec::with_capacity(self.writes.len());\n        for (k, v) in &self.writes {\n            mutations.push(Mutation {\n                key: k.clone(),\n                value: v.clone(),\n            });\n        }\n        mutations.sort_by(|a, b| a.key.cmp(&b.key));\n\n        let first = g.store.append_mutations(new_version, &mutations)?;\n        g.store.publish(new_version, first)?;\n\n        // 4. Publish in memory only after durability.\n        for m in &mutations {\n            let entry = KeyEntry {\n                version: new_version,\n                value: m.value.clone(),\n            };\n            g.history\n                .entry(m.key.clone())\n                .or_default()\n                .push(entry.clone());\n            g.current.insert(m.key.clone(), entry);\n        }\n        g.latest = new_version;\n        Ok(new_version)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for WriteTxn {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        // Uncommitted transactions leave no state behind (their buffered data\n        // frames, if any were appended, are discarded as dead bytes — but\n        // append only happens after the conflict check inside commit()).\n        let _ = &mut self.finished;\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nfn record_for<'a>(parsed: &'a ParsedFile, offset: u64) -> Option<&'a Record> {\n    parsed.records.iter().find(|r| r.offset == offset)\n}\n"},"name":"Write","type":"tool_use"}],"id":"msg_0cd11592f8bc767d3242b796","model":"auto_model/urm","role":"assistant","stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"type":"message","usage":{"input_tokens":1056,"cache_creation_input_tokens":0,"cache_read_input_tokens":70456,"output_tokens":5652,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"","iterations":[],"speed":"standard"},"stop_details":null},"wireToolInputs":{"call_8r0kjo909t1u2wlvm04rq9u2":{"content":"//! {"parentUuid":"fd9ece7a-f2b0-497c-8b36-0687e4608380","isSidechain":false,"message":{"content":[{"id":"call_g0rcdcjxpgz368nro41c92kf","input":{"file_path":"/home/admin/Downloads/biaozhul/opp3/a/src/json.rs","content":"//! Tiny dependency-free JSON implementation: just enough for the HTTP API\n//! (objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, null). Input is trusted to be\n//! a syntactically valid JSON object; malformed input yields an error.\n\nuse std::collections::BTreeMap;\n\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub enum Json {\n    Null,\n    Bool(bool),\n    /// Parsed into i64 when integral, otherwise f64.\n    Int(i64),\n    Float(f64),\n    Str(String),\n    Arr(Vec<Json>),\n    Obj(BTreeMap<String, Json>),\n}\n\nimpl Json {\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> Option<&str> {\n        match self {\n            Json::Str(s) => Some(s),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n    pub fn as_object(&self) -> Option<&BTreeMap<String, Json>> {\n        match self {\n            Json::Obj(o) => Some(o),\n            _ => None,\n        }\n    }\n    pub fn get(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&Json> {\n        self.as_object().and_then(|o| o.get(key))\n    }\n    pub fn from_bytes(b: &[u8]) -> Result<Json, String> {\n        let s = std::str::from_utf8(b).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;\n        let mut p = Parser {\n            chars: s.chars().collect(),\n            pos: 0,\n        };\n        p.skip_ws();\n        let v = p.parse_value()?;\n        p.skip_ws();\n        if p.pos != p.chars.len() {\n            return Err(format!(\"trailing data at {}\", p.pos));\n        }\n        Ok(v)\n    }\n\n    pub fn to_string_compact(&self) -> String {\n        let mut out = String::new();\n        self.write(&mut out);\n        out\n    }\n\n    fn write(&self, out: &mut String) {\n        match self {\n            Json::Null => out.push_str(\"null\"),\n            Json::Bool(b) => out.push_str(if *b { \"true\" } else { \"false\" }),\n            Json::Int(n) => out.push_str(&n.to_string()),\n            Json::Float(n) => out.push_str(&n.to_string()),\n            Json::Str(s) => write_json_string(s, out),\n            Json::Arr(a) => {\n                out.push('[');\n                for (i, v) in a.iter().enumerate() {\n                    if i > 0 {\n                        out.push(',');\n                    }\n                    v.write(out);\n                }\n                out.push(']');\n            }\n            Json::Obj(o) => {\n                out.push('{');\n                for (i, (k, v)) in o.iter().enumerate() {\n                    if i > 0 {\n                        out.push(',');\n                    }\n                    write_json_string(k, out);\n                    out.push(':');\n                    v.write(out);\n                }\n                out.push('}');\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nfn write_json_string(s: &str, out: &mut String) {\n    out.push('\"');\n    for c in s.chars() {\n        match c {\n            '\"' => out.push_str(\"\\\\\\\"\"),\n            '\\\\' => out.push_str(\"\\\\\\\\\"),\n            '\\n' => out.push_str(\"\\\\n\"),\n            '\\r' => out.push_str(\"\\\\r\"),\n            '\\t' => out.push_str(\"\\\\t\"),\n            '\\u{08}' => out.push_str(\"\\\\b\"),\n            '\\u{0c}' => out.push_str(\"\\\\f\"),\n            c if (c as u32) < 0x20 => out.push_str(&format!(\"\\\\u{:04x}\", c as u32)),\n            c => out.push(c),\n        }\n    }\n    out.push('\"');\n}\n\nstruct Parser {\n    chars: Vec<char>,\n    pos: usize,\n}\n\nimpl Parser {\n    fn skip_ws(&mut self) {\n        while self.pos < self.chars.len() && self.chars[self.pos].is_whitespace() {\n Local HTTP validation server.\n//!\n//! Thread-per-connection, JSON in/out. The binary in `src/main.rs` is only a\n//! local verification entry point — there is intentionally no frontend.\n//!\n//! ## API\n//!\n//! | Method & path                | Body                          | Meaning |\n//! |------------------------------|-------------------------------|---------|\n//! | `POST /tx/read`              | `{}`                          | open a snapshot read txn |\n//! | `GET  /tx/read/{id}/get?key=`| –                             | consistent read |\n//! | `POST /tx/read/{id}/release` | `{}`                          | release the snapshot |\n//! | `POST /tx/write`             | `{}`                          | begin a write txn |\n//! | `PUT  /tx/write/{id}`        | `{\"ops\":[{\"put\":{\"k\":..,\"v\":..}},{\"del\":{\"k\":..}}]}` | buffer writes |\n//! | `POST /tx/write/{id}/commit` | `{}`                          | commit (409 on conflict) |\n//! | `POST /tx/write/{id}/abort`  | `{}`                          | discard |\n//! | `POST /gc`                   | `{}`                          | run reclamation |\n//! | `GET  /stats`                | –                             | versions, snapshots, bytes |\n//! | `GET  /get?key=`             | –                             | one-shot latest read |\n\nuse std::collections::HashMap;\nuse std::io::{Read, Write};\nuse std::net::{TcpListener, TcpStream};\nuse std::path::Path;\nuse std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};\nuse std::thread;\n\nuse crate::json::{obj, s, Json};\nuse crate::mvcc::{CommitError, Engine, ReadTxn, WriteTxn};\n\nstruct ReadEntry(ReadTxn);\nstruct WriteEntry(WriteTxn);\n\nstruct ServerState {\n    engine: Engine,\n    reads: HashMap<u64, ReadEntry>,\n    writes: HashMap<u64, WriteEntry>,\n    next_read: u64,\n    next_write: u64,\n}\n\npub struct Server {\n    state: Arc<Mutex<ServerState>>,\n}\n\nimpl Server {\n    pub fn new(dir: &Path) -> std::io::Result<Server> {\n        let engine = Engine::open(dir)?;\n        Ok(Server {\n            state: Arc::new(Mutex::new(ServerState {\n                engine,\n                reads: HashMap::new(),\n                writes: HashMap::new(),\n                next_read: 1,\n                next_write: 1,\n            })),\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Bind and serve until the process is killed. Returns the bound address.\n    pub fn serve(&self, addr: &str) -> std::io::Result<std::net::SocketAddr> {\n        let listener = TcpListener::bind(addr)?;\n        let bound = listener.local_addr()?;\n        let state = self.state.clone();\n        thread::spawn(move || {\n            for stream in listener.incoming() {\n                match stream {\n                    Ok(stream) => {\n                        let state = state.clone();\n                        thread::spawn(move || {\n                            let _ = handle(stream, state);\n                        });\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => continue,\n                }\n            }\n        });\n        Ok(bound)\n    }\n\n    /// Engine handle for tests that want to inspect state directly.\n    pub fn engine(&self) -> Engine {\n        self.state.lock().unwrap().engine.clone()\n    }\n}\n\nfn handle(mut stream: TcpStream, state: Arc<Mutex<ServerState>>) -> std::io::Result<()> {\n    let mut head = [0u8; 4096];\n    let n = stream.read(&mut head)?;\n    if n == 0 {\n        return Ok(());\n    }\n    let head = String::from_utf8_lossy(&head[..n]).to_string();\n    let mut lines = head.split(\"\\r\\n\");\n    let request_line = lines.next().unwrap_or(\"\");\n    let mut parts = request_line.split_whitespace();\n    let method = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"\").to_string();\n    let target = parts.next().unwrap_or(\"/\").to_string();\n\n    // Read the rest of the body if Content-Length says there is more.\n    let (headers, mut body) = split_head_body(&head);\n    let clen: usize = headers\n        .iter()\n        .find_map(|(k, v)| {\n            if k.eq_ignore_ascii_case(\"content-length\") {\n                v.parse().ok()\n            } else {\n                None\n            }\n        })\n        .unwrap_or(0);\n    while body.len() < clen {\n        let mut buf = vec![0u8; clen - body.len()];\n        let r = stream.read(&mut buf)?;\n        if r == 0 {\n            break;\n        }\n        body.extend_from_slice(&buf[..r]);\n    }\n\n    let (status, json) = route(&method, &target, &body, &state);\n    let text = json.to_string_compact();\n    write!(\n        stream,\n        \"HTTP/1.1 {status}\\r\\nContent-Type: application/json\\r\\nContent-Length: {}\\r\\nConnection: close\\r\\n\\r\\n{}\",\n        text.len(),\n        text\n    )?;\n    Ok(())\n}\n\nfn split_head_body(head: &str) -> (Vec<(String, String)>, Vec<u8>) {\n    if let Some(idx) = head.find(\"\\r\\n\\r\\n\") {\n        let header_block = &head[..idx];\n        let body = head[idx + 4..].as_bytes().to_vec();\n        let mut lines = header_block.split(\"\\r\\n\");\n        lines.next(); // request line\n        let headers = lines\n            .filter_map(|l| {\n                let (k, v) = l.split_once(':')?;\n                Some((k.trim().to_string(), v.trim().to_string()))\n            })\n            .collect();\n        (headers, body)\n    } else {\n        (Vec::new(), Vec::new())\n    }\n}\n\ntype Resp = (u16, &'static str);\nconst OK: Resp = (200, \"OK\");\nconst CONFLICT: Resp = (409, \"Conflict\");\nconst BAD: Resp = (400, \"Bad Request\");\nconst NOTFOUND: Resp = (404, \"Not Found\");\nconst SERVERERR: Resp = (500, \"Internal Server Error\");\n\nfn route(method: &str, target: &str, body: &[u8], state: &Arc<Mutex<ServerState>>) -> (Resp, Json) {\n    let (path, query) = target.split_once('?').unwrap_or((target, \"\"));\n    let segments: Vec<&str> = path.trim_start_matches('/').split('/').collect();\n\n    let result = match (method, segments.as_slice()) {\n        (\"GET\", [\"get\"]) => {\n            let key = parse_query(query, \"key\");\n            match key {\n                Some(k) => {\n                    let st = state.lock().unwrap();\n                    match st.engine.get_latest(k.as_bytes()) {\n                        Some(v) => Ok((OK, obj(&[(\"found\", Json::Bool(true)), (\"key\", s(k)), (\"value\", s(String::from_utf8_lossy(&v)))]))),\n                        None => Ok((OK, obj(&[(\"found\", Json::Bool(false)), (\"key\", s(k))]))),\n                    }\n                }\n                None => Err((BAD, \"missing key\")),\n            }\n        }\n        (\"POST\", [\"tx\", \"read\"]) => {\n            let mut st = state.lock().unwrap();\n            let tx = st.engine.begin_read();\n            let id = st.next_read;\n            st.next_read += 1;\n            let version = tx.version();\n            st.reads.insert(id, ReadEntry(tx));\n            Ok((OK, obj(&[(\"read_txn_id\", Json::Int(id as i64)), (\"version\", Json::Int(version as i64))])))\n        }\n        (\"GET\", [\"tx\", \"read\", id, \"get\"]) => {\n            let id: u64 = match id.parse() {\n                Ok(v) => v,\n                Err(_) => return (BAD, s(\"bad read txn id\")),\n            };\n            let key = match parse_query(query, \"key\") {\n                Some(k) => k,\n                None => return (BAD, s(\"missing key\")),\n            };\n            let st = state.lock().unwrap();\n            match st.reads.get(&id) {\n                Some(tx) => match tx.0.get(key.as_bytes()) {\n                    Some(v) => (OK, obj(&[(\"found\", Json::Bool(true)), (\"key\", s(key)), (\"value\", s(String::from_utf8_lossy(&v)))])),\n                    None => (OK, obj(&[(\"found\", Json::Bool(false)), (\"key\", s(key))])),\n                },\n                None => (NOTFOUND, s(\"unknown read txn\")),\n            }\n        }\n        (\"POST\", [\"tx\", \"read\", id, \"release\"]) => {\n            let id: u64 = match id.parse() {\n                Ok(v) => v,\n                Err(_) => return (BAD, s(\"bad read txn id\")),\n            };\n            let mut st = state.lock().unwrap();\n            match st.reads.remove(&id) {\n                Some(tx) => {\n                    drop(tx);\n                    (OK, obj(&[(\"released\", Json::Bool(true)), (\"read_txn_id\", Json::Int(id as i64))]))\n                }\n                None => (NOTFOUND, s(\"unknown read txn\")),\n            }\n        }\n        (\"POST\", [\"tx\", \"write\"]) => {\n            let mut st = state.lock().unwrap();\n            let tx = st.engine.begin_write();\n            let id = st.next_write;\n            st.next_write += 1;\n            let version = tx.snapshot_version();\n            st.writes.insert(id, WriteEntry(tx));\n            (OK, obj(&[(\"write_txn_id\", Json::Int(id as i64)), (\"snapshot_version\", Json::Int(version as i64))]))\n        }\n        (\"PUT\", [\"tx\", \"write\", id]) => {\n            let id: u64 = match id.parse() {\n                Ok(v) => v,\n                Err(_) => return (BAD, s(\"bad write txn id\")),\n            };\n            let parsed = match Json::from_bytes(body) {\n                Ok(j) => j,\n                Err(e) => return (BAD, s(format!(\"bad json: {e}\"))),\n            };\n            let ops = match parsed.get(\"ops\").and_then(|o| match o {\n                Json::Arr(a) => Some(a),\n                _ => None,\n            }) {\n                Some(a) => a,\n                None => return (BAD, s(\"expected {\\\"ops\\\":[...]}\")),\n            };\n            let mut st = state.lock().unwrap();\n            let tx = match st.writes.get_mut(&id) {\n                Some(tx) => tx,\n                None => return (NOTFOUND, s(\"unknown write txn\")),\n            };\n            for op in ops {\n                if let Some(put) = op.get(\"put\") {\n                    let k = match put.get(\"k\").and_then(|x| x.as_str()) {\n                        Some(k) => k,\n                        None => return (BAD, s(\"put needs k\")),\n                    };\n                    let v = match put.get(\"v\").and_then(|x| x.as_str()) {\n                        Some(v) => v,\n                        None => return (BAD, s(\"put needs v\")),\n                    };\n                    tx.0.put(k.as_bytes().to_vec(), v.as_bytes().to_vec());\n                } else if let Some(del) = op.get(\"del\") {\n                    let k = match del.get(\"k\").and_then(|x| x.as_str()) {\n                        Some(k) => k,\n                        None => return (BAD, s(\"del needs k\")),\n                    };\n                    tx.0.del(k.as_bytes().to_vec());\n                } else {\n                    return (BAD, s(\"unknown op\"));\n                }\n            }\n            (OK, obj(&[(\"buffered\", Json::Int(ops.len() as i64)), (\"write_txn_id\", Json::Int(id as i64))]))\n        }\n        (\"POST\", [\"tx\", \"write\", id, \"commit\"]) => {\n            let id: u64 = match id.parse() {\n                Ok(v) => v,\n                Err(_) => return (BAD, s(\"bad write txn id\")),\n            };\n            let mut st = state.lock().unwrap();\n            let tx = match st.writes.remove(&id) {\n                Some(tx) => tx,\n                None => return (NOTFOUND, s(\"unknown write txn\")),\n            };\n            match tx.0.commit() {\n                Ok(version) => (OK, obj(&[(\"committed\", Json::Bool(true)), (\"version\", Json::Int(version as i64))])),\n                Err(CommitError::Conflict { keys }) => {\n                    let keys: Vec<Json> = keys\n                        .iter()\n                        .map(|k| s(String::from_utf8_lossy(k)))\n                        .collect();\n                    (CONFLICT, obj(&[\n                        (\"committed\", Json::Bool(false)),\n                        (\"error\", s(\"write-write conflict\")),\n                        (\"keys\", Json::Arr(keys)),\n                    ]))\n                }\n                Err(CommitError::Io(e)) => (SERVERERR, s(format!(\"io: {e}\"))),\n            }\n        }\n        (\"POST\", [\"tx\", \"write\", id, \"abort\"]) => {\n            let id: u64 = match id.parse() {\n                Ok(v) => v,\n                Err(_) => return (BAD, s(\"bad write txn id\")),\n            };\n            let mut st = state.lock().unwrap();\n            match st.writes.remove(&id) {\n                Some(_) => (OK, obj(&[(\"aborted\", Json::Bool(true))])),\n                None => (NOTFOUND, s(\"unknown write txn\")),\n            }\n        }\n        (\"POST\", [\"gc\"]) => {\n            let st = state.lock().unwrap();\n            match st.engine.gc() {\n                Ok(Some(r)) => (OK, obj(&[\n                    (\"ran\", Json::Bool(true)),\n                    (\"watermark\", Json::Int(r.watermark as i64)),\n                    (\"bytes_before\", Json::Int(r.bytes_before as i64)),\n                    (\"bytes_after\", Json::Int(r.bytes_after as i64)),\n                    (\"reclaimed\", Json::Int(r.reclaimed as i64)),\n                ])),\n                Ok(None) => (OK, obj(&[(\"ran\", Json::Bool(false)), (\"reason\", s(\"nothing to reclaim at current watermark\"))])),\n                Err(e) => (SERVERERR, s(format!(\"gc failed: {e}\"))),\n            }\n        }\n        (\"GET\", [\"stats\"]) => {\n            let st = state.lock().unwrap();\n            let stats = st.engine.stats();\n            (OK, stats_json(&stats))\n        }\n        _ => (NOTFOUND, s(\"no such route\")),\n    };\n\n    match result {\n        Ok(resp) | Err(resp) => resp,\n    }\n}\n\nfn stats_json(st: &crate::mvcc::Stats) -> Json {\n    let snaps: Vec<Json> = st\n        .snapshots\n        .iter()\n        .map(|si| {\n            obj(&[\n                (\"id\", Json::Int(si.id as i64)),\n                (\"version\", Json::Int(si.version as i64)),\n            ])\n        })\n        .collect();\n    obj(&[\n        (\"latest_version\", Json::Int(st.latest_version as i64)),\n        (\"committed_versions\", Json::Int(st.committed_versions as i64)),\n        (\"live_keys\", Json::Int(st.live_keys as i64)),\n        (\"watermark\", Json::Int(st.watermark as i64)),\n        (\"file_bytes\", Json::Int(st.file_bytes as i64)),\n        (\"retained_bytes\", Json::Int(st.retained_bytes as i64)),\n        (\"reclaimable_bytes\", Json::Int(st.reclaimable_bytes as i64)),\n        (\"snapshots\", Json::Arr(snaps)),\n    ])\n}\n\nfn parse_query(query: &str, key: &str) -> Option<String> {\n    for pair in query.split('&') {\n        let (k, v) = pair.split_once('=')?;\n        if k == key {\n            return Some(percent_decode(v));\n        }\n    }\n    None\n}\n\nfn percent_decode(s: &str) -> String {\n    let bytes = s.as_bytes();\n    let mut out = Vec::with_capacity(bytes.len());\n    let mut i = 0;\n    while i < bytes.len() {\n        if bytes[i] == b'%' && i + 2 < bytes.len() {\n            let h = |b: u8| match b {\n                b'0'..=b'9' => Some(b - b'0'),\n                b'a'..=b'f' => Some(b - b'a' + 10),\n                b'A'..=b'F' => Some(b - b'A' + 10),\n                _ => None,\n {\n                    return (BAD, s(\"unknown op\"));\n                }\n            }\n            (OK, obj(&[(\"buffered\", Json::Int(ops.len() as i64)), (\"write_txn_id\", Json::Int(id as
